title: Tire tracks: ruts from speed, scuffs from real contact slip
summary: Enhanced/High tire tracks now follow the physics contact. The simulation reports per-wheel contact slip (sideways scrub and tread minus ground speed in the tire force frame; presentation only). Soft mud ruts under any rolling wheel; firm dirt/snow only take a faint press at speed and nothing when slow. Slides, wheelspin and lockup tear wider untreaded scuffs that fade when the tire grips again. Marks multiply the lit ground (2×) with world-space breakup instead of flat black.
details: Discovery: the original wheel model never slips longitudinally while rolling; tread speed only departs from ground speed when braking locks a wheel on low-braking surfaces or throttle spins it on low-drive surfaces. Measured slip on env01: straight/gripping ~0–3 ft/s, full-lock slides 12–30 ft/s, wheelspin up to ~17 ft/s.
Graphics unit tests, atv-core (487) and atv-web Rust tests, fmt/clippy, test_graphics_presets.mjs browser test; local Playwright drives on env01/env02/env04 with before/after screenshots.
limitation: Host-only screenshots; thresholds tuned by eye; player quad only (not CPU racers, remote riders or motorcycles); no mud-map screenshot yet.
caption: Enhanced tire tracks on env01: patchy streaked slide marks starting only where the tires broke loose (new), compared to old uniform thin dark lines on every path.
